question: Which blood vessels carry deoxygenated blood away from the heart?
explanation: While most arteries carry oxygen-rich blood, the pulmonary arteries are an exception because they pump oxygen-poor blood from the heart to the lungs. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h1)

question: Why must the walls of arteries be built to handle high pressure?

options.A: Because blood is pumped directly out of the heart's ventricles
options.B: So they can store excess blood volume during low activity
options.C: To prevent the backflow of blood into the capillary beds
options.D: To filter out waste products before reaching the kidneys

explanation: Arteries receive blood straight from the forceful contractions of the heart, requiring strong walls to withstand that powerful surge. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h1)

question: What is the name of the innermost lining layer of an artery?
explanation: The tunica intima is the innermost layer of the blood vessel wall, featuring a smooth lining that helps blood flow easily without clotting. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h2)

question: Which layer of the arterial wall is mainly responsible for changing vessel diameter?
explanation: The middle layer contains smooth muscle tissue that contracts or relaxes to alter the width of the artery, helping control local blood flow. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h2)

question: How do elastic arteries help smooth out the blood flow from the heart?

options.A: By narrowing completely to trap blood in the chest
options.B: By stretching during heart contraction and recoiling during relaxation
options.C: By opening valves to stop blood from flowing backward
options.D: By releasing hormones that slow down the heart rate

explanation: Elastic recoil acts like a secondary push, storing energy when the heart beats and releasing it to keep blood moving steadily between heartbeats. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h3)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an elastic artery?
explanation: The aorta and its main branches closest to the heart are classified as elastic arteries because they manage the highest pressure surges directly from the heart. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h3)

question: What is the main tissue type found in the tunica media of muscular arteries?
explanation: Muscular arteries contain thick layers of smooth muscle cells, giving them the ability to actively constrict or dilate to direct blood flow where it is needed. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h4)

question: What happens to a muscular artery when sympathetic nerve stimulation increases?

options.A: It undergoes vasoconstriction and reduces blood flow
options.B: It loses its elastic recoil completely
options.C: It stretches passively to store more blood volume
options.D: It undergoes vasodilation and increases local pressure

explanation: Sympathetic nervous system activation triggers the smooth muscle in muscular arteries to contract, narrowing the vessel and reducing blood entry. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h4)

question: Why are arterioles often referred to as resistance vessels?

options.A: They resist stretching when the heart pumps blood
options.B: They create the greatest opposition to blood flow due to their small size
options.C: They block the return of deoxygenated blood
options.D: They prevent white blood cells from entering tissues

explanation: The tiny size of arterioles creates substantial friction and resistance, which is the main factor controlling overall blood pressure in the body. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of arterioles regulating blood flow into capillary beds?

options.A: To filter waste products out of the plasma
options.B: To pump blood back up to the heart against gravity
options.C: To store extra blood volume when the person is resting
options.D: To protect fragile capillaries from high pressure and match local tissue needs

explanation: Capillaries have extremely thin walls that would rupture under high arterial pressure, making the pressure-lowering function of arterioles essential. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h5)

question: How does an increase in vascular resistance affect blood flow through an artery, assuming pressure stays the same?
explanation: Resistance works against the movement of fluid, so higher resistance means less blood can pass through the vessel. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h6)

question: Where are the primary baroreceptors located that monitor systemic blood pressure?
explanation: Specialized stretch receptors in the carotid sinus and aortic arch constantly sense blood pressure changes and send signals to the brain to adjust heart rate and vessel tone. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T13#BMP111_U5_T13_h6)
